### Executive Summary
- Active exploitation confirmed for multiple **auth-bypass flaws**: miniOrange SAML SSO (WordPress) and an **Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic Proxy Plug-in** issue added to **CISA KEV**—treat as internet-facing compromise risk.
- Government warning on **active exploitation of TeamCity Server** continues; prioritize any externally reachable CI/CD systems (high blast radius to code/signing/secrets).
- Supply-chain/phishing angle: **npm packages used as phishing infrastructure** (fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA / ClickFix-style lures); reinforce email/web controls and endpoint execution monitoring.

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) miniOrange SAML SSO (WordPress) critical auth bypasses – actively exploited**
- **What happened:** CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated auth bypasses in miniOrange SAML WP plugin (CVE-2026-61979, CVE-2026-15981) are being exploited; paid editions may require **manual patching** and were under-reported in vuln DBs.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Direct path to **admin takeover** of public web properties (credential-less), likely followed by webshell/backdoor, redirects, and lateral movement via reused credentials.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Identify WP sites using miniOrange SAML (all editions) and confirm patch/mitigation; hunt for **new admin users / unexpected logins** and **plugin/theme file changes** on WP hosts.

**2) Oracle HTTP Server / WebLogic Proxy Plug-in CVE-2026-21962 (CVSS 10) – CISA KEV**
- **What happened:** CISA added **CVE-2026-21962** to KEV, indicating **in-the-wild exploitation** affecting Oracle HTTP Server and Oracle WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Likely internet-facing middleware exposure; compromise can enable **initial access** to app tiers handling sensitive financial workflows.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Enumerate all Oracle HTTP Server/WebLogic proxy components (including behind load balancers); enforce emergency patch/mitigation and add temporary **WAF/edge rules** to reduce exposure while patching.

**3) TeamCity Server critical flaw – active exploitation warnings (gov/partners)**
- **What happened:** Australia reiterated active exploitation of a **critical TeamCity Server** vulnerability (follows prior US warnings).
- **Why it matters operationally:** CI/CD compromise enables **source/code tampering, credential/secrets theft, signing key abuse**, and rapid enterprise-wide spread.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Confirm TeamCity instances are patched and not publicly exposed; review TeamCity admin/audit events for **new users/tokens, new build agents, unusual build config changes** and rotate exposed CI secrets if suspicious activity found.

**4) Web app RCE/chain PoCs circulating (Next.js on Windows, Acelle Mail SSTI→RCE, legacy “evergreen” RCEs)**
- **What happened:** New/reshared PoCs published for high-impact web exploitation paths including **Next.js RCE on Windows-hosted deployments (CVE-2026-75604)** and **Acelle Mail unauthenticated SSTI-to-RCE chain**; additional PoCs resurfaced for older high-impact CVEs (e.g., Log4Shell, BlueKeep, Zerologon).
- **Why it matters operationally:** PoC availability drives scanning and opportunistic exploitation of **edge apps**; older “fixed” vulns still hit due to forgotten systems.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Run an exposure check for internet-facing Next.js (Windows) and Acelle Mail; increase alerting on **new web process execution** (cmd/powershell from web server context) and block/contain any host showing web-to-shell behavior.

**5) Supply-chain/phishing infrastructure via npm packages (fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA / ClickFix lures)**
- **What happened:** Researchers reported **24 npm packages** abusing unpkg mirrors to host **fake CAPTCHA** pages used for ClickFix-style social engineering.
- **Why it matters operationally:** Increases likelihood of **user-driven execution** (clipboard/paste/run, script execution) leading to infostealers and footholds; relevant to finance due to credential/session theft.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Tune email/web filtering for fake CAPTCHA/verification lures and block known malicious packages internally where possible (assumption: package names not provided in summary); hunt endpoints for **user-initiated script execution** shortly after web browsing to “verification” pages.

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **WordPress / miniOrange SSO exploitation:** Monitor web server + WP audit logs for **admin logins from new IPs**, sudden privilege changes, new users (ATT&CK **T1078 Valid Accounts**); watch file integrity on `wp-content/plugins/` and `wp-content/themes/`.
- **Oracle HTTP/WebLogic KEV:** On edge/WAF + reverse proxy logs, alert on **spikes in 4xx/5xx** and unusual requests to Oracle proxy endpoints; on hosts, detect **new processes spawned by OHS/WebLogic** (ATT&CK **T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application**, **T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter**).
- **TeamCity compromise indicators:** In TeamCity audit logs, flag **new admin accounts, API token creation, VCS root changes, build step edits**, and unexpected agent registrations (ATT&CK **T1552 Unsecured Credentials**, **T1098 Account Manipulation**).
- **Next.js/Windows web-to-RCE:** On IIS/Node hosts (EDR + Windows Security logs), alert on `node.exe`/web worker spawning `cmd.exe`, `powershell.exe`, `wscript/cscript`, or writing to web directories (ATT&CK **T1505.003 Web Shell**, **T1059.001 PowerShell**).
- **Acelle Mail / PHP command injection patterns:** On Linux EDR + web logs, detect `php-fpm`/`apache` spawning shells, unexpected outbound connections, and new cron/systemd timers (ATT&CK **T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel**, **T1053 Scheduled Task/Job**).
- **ClickFix-style phishing outcomes:** Correlate secure web gateway + EDR for **browser → clipboard → shell** sequences; alert on `powershell -enc`, `mshta`, `rundll32`, `regsvr32` shortly after visiting “captcha/verify” URLs (ATT&CK **T1204 User Execution**, **T1218 Signed Binary Proxy Execution**).
- **Internet-wide opportunistic scanning (PoC release surge):** On perimeter IDS/firewall, watch for **broad port/URL scanning** against web apps and CI endpoints; rate-limit and geo/IP reputation controls where appropriate (assumption: no specific IOCs provided).

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Asset/exposure hygiene:** Reconcile inventory for **WordPress SSO plugins (incl. paid editions), TeamCity, Oracle OHS/WebLogic proxy, Next.js on Windows**, and Acelle Mail—ensure owners and patch SLAs are assigned.
- **CI/CD hardening:** Enforce TeamCity access controls (VPN/allowlist), MFA where supported, least-privilege tokens, and routine **secret rotation**; validate build artifact signing and provenance.
- **Web app containment controls:** Standardize EDR prevent rules for **web server spawning shells**, block common LOLBins for server roles, and implement file integrity monitoring on web roots.
- **Dependency/supply-chain governance:** Add controls for **npm package allowlisting**, private registry use, and automated detection of typosquatting/malicious packages (campaign used npm as infrastructure even without direct code execution).
- **Credential/session protection:** Increase monitoring for **session cookie theft / infostealer behaviors** (unusual OAuth consent, anomalous IdP logins) given phishing lure trend; ensure conditional access policies are enforced.
- **Backlog cleanup for “old but exploited” CVEs:** Validate remediation coverage for recurring PoC’d issues (e.g., Log4Shell/BlueKeep/Zerologon class) on any legacy/isolated segments—these routinely reappear during scanning waves.
